chunks: Enjoined on you is fighting, and this you abhor. You may dislike a thing yet it may be good for you; or a thing may haply please you but may be bad for you. Only God has knowledge, and you do not know.

key_terms.عَسَى: perhaps or it may be that

ai.seo_question: Why did the Muslims dislike fighting when it was commanded in the Quran?
ai.summary: This verse, revealed in the context of the early Muslim community's hesitation to engage in battle despite the command, establishes the theological principle of *al-karhiyyah* (divine decree being good even if disliked). Shia scholars, such as Al-Tabarsi in *Majma' al-Bayan*, emphasize that this applies not only to physical combat but also to acts of worship and obedience that require effort or sacrifice, highlighting the contrast between human limited perception (*zahir*) and God's comprehensive knowledge (*batin*). It serves as a foundational text for understanding the virtue of enduring hardship in obedience to divine will.
